newsitem.title: USA: UAL says it has pact with flight attendants.
newsitem.headline: UAL says it has pact with flight attendants.

text.p: United Airlines, a unit of UAL Corp, said Monday it reached a tentative agreement on a new contract with the Association of Flight Attendants union.
The new contract, which is subject to ratification by the airline's 20,000 flight attendants, would run through the end of 2006, United said.

"To respect the AFA's need to communicate the details of the tentative agreement to its members, United will not at this time release any further information regarding specific components of the contract," the airline said.

The flight attendants' union announced earlier that it had reached agreement with the Chicago-based airline. Without providing specifics, the union said it had achieved its primary goals of getting "raises, retirement and respect."

"This tentative agreement should allow us to build a foundation of long-term growth and stability in our relationship with our flight attendants," United Chief Executive Jerry Greenwald said in a statement.

"A 10-year contract gives us the opportunity to achieve meaningful and lasting change. It also will allow us to accomplish the service revolution necessary to become the worldwide airline of choice," Greenwald said.
Ratification of the tentative agreement is expected to be completed by October, the airline said.
